answer: An agent economy annotating multimodal data, from a classical sonnet to raven calls over a grassy knoll, can resist Sybil attacks using verifiable delay functions. Each identity must compute a sequential, non-parallelizable cryptographic proof before participating. An attacker incurs the scarce physical cost of dedicated processor time and electricity per generated identity. However, this requirement imposes onboarding latency and penalizes urgent, time-sensitive agents.
